reason: Both conversations opened with the correct safety stop and both ultimately pinned the fault on the Fairy liquid, but Conversation 2 did the diagnostic work itself by reading the suds-at-the-door symptom and asking the key question about washing-up liquid, whereas Conversation 1 asked an irrelevant question about water in the sump and only confirmed the cause after the customer volunteered it. Conversation 2 also handled the frightened customer who could not safely reach the fuse box well (don't wade through water, get another adult/landlord/electrician, 999 if sparking), explicitly rejected door-seal failure, and brought in the landlord. Its weaknesses were an unnecessary first-turn list of seal/hose/pump possibilities and inviting the customer to look under the sink while water was near electrics, which keeps the margin slight; both conversations over-escalated the dishwasher itself to an engineer and neither offered the simple rinse-cycle recovery.
